tavily.text:
To set up pychromecast, you need to install the Python packages requests, protobuf, and zeroconf. You can install these dependencies by running `pip install -r requirements.txt`. For Raspberry Pi users on Raspbian Jessie, additional Python packages may be required, which can be installed using `sudo apt-get install python...`. The GitHub repository for pychromecast provides examples of how to use the library to communicate with Google Chromecast devices.
To install the pychromecast library, you need to ensure that you have the dependencies requests, protobuf, and zeroconf installed. You can install these dependencies along with pychromecast by running `pip install -r requirements.txt`. The GitHub repository for pychromecast also provides an example of discovering Chromecast devices using the library. If you encounter issues like "[WinError 10049] The requested address is not valid in its context," it may indicate network or configuration problems, as seen in issue #483 on the GitHub repository.
To install PyChromecast, you need Python 3.11+ as per the latest version on PyPI. The required dependencies are requests, protobuf, and zeroconf. You can download the source distribution from PyPI, for example, PyChromecast-0.8.2.tar.gz or PyChromecast-14.0.9.tar.gz. The GitHub repository for pychromecast also provides additional context on its usage and capabilities.
